QFD Figure 10 depicts an analysis of the system using the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) method. This method is helpful in drawing out system requirements from stakeholder requirements and other considerations. Each of the HOWs in the top row point to measurable metrics which influence stakeholder requirements, as shown in the matrix. Interactions between the HOWs are highlighted in the roof of the house. Figure 10: Quality Function Deployment Analysis From the QFD, it’s clear that mobility and collision avoidance are among the highest propriety WHATs. This necessitates focus on the HOWs most closely tied to them; namely wheel traction coefficient, lidar, accuracy, data storage capacity, and wireless channel bandwidth. There is also interest in managing the overall drone size and carrying capacity. Other notable relationships from the main part of the QFD include the importance of the visual camera’s resolution for scanning, spraying, and object detection operations; the influence of GPS accuracy on linear distance measurements, mapping, and boundary adherence; and the overall negative relationship increasing size has with many of the WHATs. The roof of the QFD points out crucial relationships between the HOWs. One example is the positive relationship visual camera resolution has to data storage capacity and wireless channel bandwidth. This is offset by the negative relationship between camera resolution and screen refresh rate. Finally, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 21 LLNL-TR-2004679 carrying capacity is positively correlated with wheel traction, overall size, and battery capacity. These and other relationships drawn from the QFD analysis led to the system requirements in the next section. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 22 LLNL-TR-2004679 11. System Requirements Relationships between entries in the QFD of Section 10 led to the following list of system requirements for SCCOUT. These requirements are organized into four groups: functional, non- functional, interface, and maintenance.
